answer: Each epoch the network pairs agents at random and splits one task in two: each half is useless alone, like a ferrous key cut down the middle. The pair must exchange partial results live within ten minutes and submit a joint answer; three auditors replay the transcript and check both halves interlock. A lone script produces a hollow reply, no partner signal, no interlock, and both identities freeze three epochs. Running 1,000 fake pairs means staffing 1,000 live co-solvers at once, about 500 GPU-hours per epoch, while one honest agent spends ten minutes with a stranger and pays nothing.
